create.name: Chungliang Al Huang
create.bio:
Chungliang Al Huang grew up in China in a family of scholars and learned tai ji, kung fu and brush calligraphy as a boy. His family moved to Taiwan in 1949, and he moved to America as a student in 1955, taking up architecture, anthropology and dance. With his wife Suzanne Pierce he ran a modern dance company before turning back to the Chinese arts he had grown up with. He has taught at Esalen every year for more than five decades, and he worked closely with Alan Watts, who wrote the foreword to his first book, Embrace Tiger, Return to Mountain, and with whom he wrote Tao: The Watercourse Way.

His own approach, which he calls Living Tao, treats tai ji as a creative and playful practice rather than a fixed sequence, mixing movement, the five elements, calligraphy, poetry, music and storytelling, and drawing on Taoist, Buddhist and Confucian thought. He founded the Living Tao Foundation, based in Gold Beach on the Oregon coast, and directs the Lan Ting Institute at Wu Yi Mountain in China. Alongside his books on tai ji he co-wrote several titles with the coach Jerry Lynch on Taoist ideas in sport. He still teaches seasonal online sessions and in person.

books.title: Embrace Tiger, Return to Mountain: The Essence of Tai Ji
books.author: Chungliang Al Huang
books.description: His first book, from 1973, drawn from his early workshops and introduced by Alan Watts. It presents tai ji as a way of living in the moment, with the author's own calligraphy and photographs by Si Chi Ko.

books.title: Essential Tai Ji
books.author: Chungliang Al Huang
books.description: A short illustrated introduction to the basic movements of tai ji and the ideas of nature, space and time behind them. Colour photographs sit alongside his brush calligraphy.

books.title: Thinking Body, Dancing Mind: Taosports for Extraordinary Performance in Athletics, Business, and Life
books.author: Chungliang Al Huang and Jerry Lynch
books.description: Written with the sports coach Jerry Lynch, this book applies Taoist principles to sport, work and everyday effort. Short chapters pair a Taoist idea with simple exercises in attitude and attention.

books.title: The Chinese Book of Animal Powers
books.author: Chungliang Al Huang
books.description: An illustrated book for readers of all ages on the Chinese tradition of animal signs tied to the year of birth, and how each animal's qualities can be learned from.

books.title: Spirit of the Dancing Warrior: Asian Wisdom for Peak Performance in Athletics and Life
books.author: Jerry Lynch and Chungliang Al Huang
books.description: A second collaboration with Jerry Lynch, framing athletic training as a warrior's path informed by Asian philosophy. It focuses on courage, steadiness and character in competition.

books.title: The Way of the Champion: Lessons from Sun Tzu's the Art of War and Other Tao Wisdom for Sports & Life
books.author: Jerry Lynch and Chungliang Al Huang
books.description: Lynch and Huang draw on Sun Tzu and other Chinese classics to offer short lessons for athletes and coaches on strategy, teamwork and self-mastery.

books.title: Working Out, Working Within: The Tao of Inner Fitness Through Sports and Exercise
books.author: Jerry Lynch and Chungliang Al Huang
books.description: A guide to treating regular exercise as a reflective practice, using Taoist ideas to bring more awareness and enjoyment to training.

courses.title: The Essential Qigong of China: The Energy, the Movement, and the Stories
courses.description: A weekend at Esalen introducing a core set of qigong exercises for beginners and newer practitioners. He teaches through metaphor, visualisation, chanting and breathing, and tells the history of the practice along the way.

courses.title: Creative Tai Ji Experience: Change, Transformation, Metamorphosis
courses.description: A week at Esalen in which students improvise on traditional tai ji forms, the five elements and old ritual movements. Open to all levels, it mixes practice with his storytelling and qigong.

courses.title: 2nd Circle and Essential Core Learning
courses.description: A 49-minute recording from a summer seminar in Gold Beach, Oregon. He demonstrates and teaches the second circle of the Living Tao form together with related calligraphy and ideas.

courses.title: Living Tao Wu Xing 五行 Five Moving Forces of Nature
courses.description: A 28-minute video in which he explains and shows the five elements of Chinese thought through symbol, image and movement.

courses.title: Wei Wu Wei
courses.description: A 25-minute talk on the Taoist idea of acting without forcing and how it shapes tai ji practice.

courses.title: Metaphors: Five Moving Forces
courses.description: A short film of the five elements sequence and the first circle, performed in the gardens of Lotusland in Santa Barbara.

courses.title: Living Tao Forest Bathing Meditation
courses.description: A nine-minute guided meditation among trees, based on the East Asian custom of forest bathing.

free_resources.title: LIVING TAO TAI JI at Wu Yi Mountain
free_resources.description: A feature-length film by Guido Ferrari, free from the foundation's store. It shows the tai ji ritual, the five elements and the three circles of his form, each with his commentary.

free_resources.title: TAO: The Watercourse Way at Wu Yi Mountain
free_resources.description: A companion film, also free, in which he talks about the Tao in daily life, non-forcing action and the heroic journey, with calligraphy and readings of classical Chinese poems.
